# Testament of Simeon — 2
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** A copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph also died. **2** For Simeon fell sick, and his sons came to visit him. And being strengthened he sat up and kissed them, and said unto them: **3** Hearken, ye children, to Simeon your father, and I will declare unto you the things which I have in my heart. **4** I was born of Jacob, the second son of my father, and Leah my mother called me Simeon, because the Lord had heard her prayer. **5** I became strong exceedingly; I drew not back from any deed, nor was I afraid of anything; for my heart was hard, and my liver was unmoved, and my bowels were without compassion. **6** Because also valour had been given to me from the Most High, through works of might and fortitude of heart.

**2** And I became jealous of Joseph, for our father loved him above all. **2** And I set my mind to slay him, because the prince of error sent forth the spirit of jealousy, and blinded my mind, so that I regarded him not as a brother, and spared not even Jacob my father. **3** But his God and the God of our fathers sent his angel and delivered him out of my hands. **4** For when I went to Shechem to fetch ointment for the flocks, and Reuben to Dothan, where were our stores and all our provisions, Judah our brother sold him to the Ishmaelites. **5** And when Reuben heard these things he was grieved, for he wished to restore him to his father. **6** But I had been jealous and had not consented to sell him, but had kept him seven days; for while I was away Judah had sold him. **7** And I grieved in my soul over him for many days, for I had done a great sin. **8** And Jacob our father sought for him continually; and Leah our mother and all our brethren mourned and were distressed. **9** But I alone rejoiced not, for the spirit of jealousy had hardened my heart. **10** Then after two years I heard that Joseph had been sold into Egypt, and I mourned bitterly; and I repented with great grief before the Lord.

**3** Now therefore, my children, take heed to yourselves concerning all the works of jealousy; for jealousy ruleth over the whole mind of man, and suffereth him not to eat, or to drink, or to do any good thing. **2** But it ever constraineth him to destroy him that he envieth; and so long as he that is envied flourisheth, he that envieth fadeth away. **3** Two years therefore I afflicted my soul, and was weakened in my limbs, and became feeble; for I had the spirit of jealousy in me. **4** And I knew that what had befallen me was from the Lord, and I repented and wept; and I prayed before God with my whole heart that the plague of jealousy might be removed from me. **5** And he showed me that because of Joseph I had done this, and I was healed.

**4** Now therefore, my children, love ye each one his brother, and put away from you the spirit of jealousy; for this spirit maketh savage the soul, and destroyeth the body, it causeth rage and war in the mind, and stirreth up unto deeds of blood, and leadeth the mind astray, and suffereth it not to act with equity. **2** For even unto our father Judah the Lord gave understanding and long-suffering; for he was among the most merciful of us, and he would have put away the jealousy against Joseph, but the spirit of jealousy in Simeon his brother prevailed. **3** Beware therefore of jealousy, my children, and love one another with good heart; **4** and tell ye also these things to your children, that they honour Judah and Levi, for from them shall the Lord raise up salvation to Israel.

**5** For the Lord will raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Judah as it were a King, God and man, He shall save all the Gentiles and the race of Israel. **2** Therefore do ye also, my children, obey Levi and Judah, and be ye not lifted up against these two tribes; for from them shall arise your salvation. **3** For the Lord shall choose from Levi a first priest, and from Judah a king who shall rule over all; and shall make peace between the two, and they shall serve the Lord. **4** For I charge you to fear the Lord your God with your whole heart, and to walk in simplicity according to all his law. **5** And teach your sons letters, that they may have understanding all their life, reading unceasingly the law of God. **6** For everyone that knoweth the law of the Lord shall be honoured, and shall not be a stranger whithersoever he goeth.

**6** And many friends shall he have more than his parents, and many men will desire to serve him, and to hear the law from his mouth. **2** Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon earth, that ye may have a treasure in heaven. **3** And sow good things in your souls, that ye may find them in your life. **4** But if ye sow evil things, ye shall reap every trouble and affliction. **5** Get wisdom in the fear of God with diligence; for if there be a captivity, and cities and lands be laid waste, and gold and silver and every possession perish, nothing can take away the wisdom of the wise, save the blindness of ungodliness and the dulness that cometh of sin. **6** For if one keep himself from these evil things, then even among his enemies shall wisdom be a glory to him, and in a strange country a fatherland, and in the midst of foes shall prove a friend.

**7** Whosoever teacheth these things and doeth them shall be enthroned with kings, as was also Joseph our brother. **2** Therefore, my children, I have shown you everything, and the whole story of my repentance. **3** And remember that I kept Joseph in ward seven days; and my father was grieving for me, and I did not weep. **4** And the Lord afflicted my loins with sickness for seven months; and I knew that this was because of Joseph. **5** And I repented, and mourned before the Lord for seven days also; and after this he had compassion upon me, and I recovered my health.

---
*End of Testament of Simeon*
